title: The git mailbox tells a sender whether its message was read
why: Owner 09:06 CST Nov 13, relayed by the retrospective, his words: "D20 -- i'm pretty sure read receipts exist, and anyways we're leaving anthropic's messaging system for our own right? can't we add read receipts there". So D20 (no read receipt) is built in our own mailbox, not raised upstream.
source: owner 09:06 CST Nov 13 via retrospective 09:07 CST
note: Shape (retrospective): mail take already removes the message file in a commit on refs/heads/mail, so a command such as mail status <id> can print open, or taken with the time and taker, read from git. Homes: decision session-messages, hooks/mail.py. Check, red first: a taken message reads taken with its taker; an untaken one reads open. Lint re-run PASS at 29c9b8462, #3137 handed to the batch runner (lane 10:44 CST Nov 13). Notes for the notes file: (1) StatusCommand in hooks/test_mail.py has no no-write or read-count assert in a case that runs on Windows; one assert that store.tip() is unchanged in test_untaken_message_reads_open_exit_0 would cover it. (2) Surviving mutant: dropping the leading "/" in message_status's name match makes a suffix id read open; add a suffix id to test_unknown_id_reads_unknown_exit_1_and_never_open. (3) Surviving mutant: stamped[-1] to stamped[0] passes; add a done file with a quoted Taken-by line ahead of the real stamp. (4) check_unknown_reads_contract has no mail member, so it does not cover status.
